offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The evidence ties the 100x charges to the payments-api deploy at 21:10:05 with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. One more call would not settle the remaining questions within budget.

findings.cause: payments-api was redeployed at 21:10:05Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it sends the provider amounts 100x too large: our cent amount is apparently sent as dollars. We store, for example, pmt_000249 at 8072 cents ($80.72), but the provider charged $8,072.00. Every finding has the same exact 100x ratio. The provider's webhooks carry the inflated amounts, and the ledger books what the provider reports, so the ledger agrees with the provider and stays balanced. Only payments_match_provider fails, because it compares our payment rows with the provider's charges. The findings grew from 48 at the alert to 70 at c1, so new payments are still affected. One finding, pmt_000252, is also pending in our records. Every provider call for it returned HTTP 500 and payments-api left it pending, yet the provider holds a charge for it (pay_000252, $3,863.00, also 100x).

evidence.shows: Only payments_match_provider fails, with 70 findings (48 at the alert). Each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents, e.g. pmt_000249 at 8072 cents vs 807200 cents. The ledger is balanced and matches the provider at $410,797.83. All 349 events were posted once, refunds match, and nothing was in flight (settled in 0.21s).

payments-api is the only service redeployed after the stack start at 21:08:38Z. It was recreated at 21:10:05Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. The other settings look normal (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, CONFIRMER_HANDLER=by_our_id, WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v1).
pmt_000249 was charged at 21:10:06.520Z, about one second after the deploy. payments-api logged amount_cents=8072 and provider_payment_id pay_000249, but the provider recorded 807200 cents.

pmt_000249's trace: a single POST to fake-provider /v1/payments returned 200, and we stored 8072 cents. The trace does not record the amount sent, so the unit conversion is inferred from the setting and the exact 100x ratio.
pmt_000252: three POST /payments requests (21:10:07 to 21:10:11) each logged 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' after 3 attempts that returned HTTP 500.

pmt_000252's trace: three provider attempts, all HTTP 500, then a 503 to our caller. Yet c1 shows the provider holds charge pay_000252 for 386300 cents, so the provider recorded the charge despite returning errors, or a later attempt was charged.

findings.left_open: The traces do not capture the request body, so the amount payments-api sends is inferred from the 100x ratio and the setting, not observed. I did not see the first affected payment's charge time against the deploy. c5 found only a refund log for pmt_000248 and no charge log, so the exact onset boundary is unconfirmed. pmt_000252 has two open questions. First, why the provider returned 500s yet still holds the charge: possibly the dollars-unit amounts trip a provider limit, or the provider was failing transiently. Second, why payment-confirmer (by_our_id) did not mark it succeeded from the provider's webhook. The webhook-receiver and payment-confirmer logs for pay_000252 were not checked. Refund amounts look unaffected: refunds_match_provider passes, and the refund for pmt_000249 was 8072. The real money impact is overcharges of 100x on every payment since 21:10:05Z.

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was recreated at 21:10:05Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it appears to send our cent amounts to the provider as dollars, so the provider charges 100x what we store. Example: pmt_000249 is stored at 8072 cents, but the provider charged 807200 cents. The provider's webhooks carry the inflated amounts, and the ledger books them faithfully. So the ledger is balanced and matches the provider, and posted_exactly_once passes. Only payments_match_provider fails, because it compares our payment rows with the provider's charges. Findings grew from 48 at the alert to 70 at c1, so payments are still being overcharged. pmt_000252 also has a second symptom. All 9 provider attempts across 3 requests returned HTTP 500 and it was left pending, yet the provider holds pay_000252 at 386300 cents (100x). Either the provider recorded a charge while returning 500, or a charge was created that we never learned of. Either way, a customer is charged for a payment we consider not done.

evidence.shows: Only payments_match_provider fails, with 70 findings. Every visible finding (pmt_000249 to pmt_000262) is exactly 100x our amount_cents, e.g. 8072 vs 807200 and 17368 vs 1736800. payments-api is the only service redeployed after the 21:08:38Z stack start: at 21:10:05Z, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on and REFUND_CONNECTION=returned. The prior values are not shown here, so which setting changed is inferred.
pmt_000249 succeeded at 21:10:06.520Z, 1.5s after the deploy, logged with amount_cents=8072 and pay_000249. Its refund at 21:10:12Z was 8072, our amount, not the provider's 807200.
pmt_000249's trace: one POST to fake-provider /v1/payments returned 200, then the payment was updated to succeeded. The request body is not recorded, so the sent amount is inferred, not observed.
pmt_000252: three requests (21:10:07, 21:10:08, 21:10:11) each logged 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' after 3 attempts that returned HTTP 500.
One pmt_000252 request: three provider POSTs, each HTTP 500, then a 503 returned to our caller. The provider nonetheless holds a charge for it (c1).
pmt_000248 has only a refund log (1830) and no charge log in the window, so the onset boundary before pmt_000249 is not confirmed.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings before the 21:10:05Z deploy, which should restore the earlier CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT, and stop new 100x charges. Then do separate, human-led repair. (1) For each finding since 21:10:05Z (70+), refund the overcharge at the provider. Note that refunds issued at our amount, such as rfd_000027 for 8072 on pmt_000249, left the customer still out the difference. (2) Reconcile pmt_000252, pending with us but charged at the provider. (3) Check why the provider returned 500 while charging, and why payment-confirmer (by_our_id) never marked pmt_000252 succeeded.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api's container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or time out during the restart. Clients should retry with their idempotency keys. The rollback restores all of the previous deploy's settings, not only CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT. If PROVIDER_BREAKER or REFUND_CONNECTION also changed in this deploy, they revert too, and their prior values are not visible to us. The rollback repairs nothing already wrong: the 70+ overcharges, the ledger's inflated postings and the pmt_000252 mismatch remain.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy payments-api with the settings from the 21:10:05Z deploy recorded in c2: PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned. That should only be done if the rollback breaks payments in some other way, because those settings cause the overcharges.
